text:
maria: heads up — we're seeing a sustained eviction spike in ap-southeast1-b starting ~09:10 UTC. small-gpu pods are being scheduled in clumps on a handful of racks, leaving medium/large jobs pending. looks like 'bunching' + taint/late-attach delay = evict churn. ops-bot flagged 120 evictions in 20m.

ops-bot: [automated] eviction-spike detected: 120 evictions in 20m for cluster gpu-prod-ap-se1. alert: #infra oncall

ajay: digging in — attaching scheduler debug for the window:
```
I0315 09:10:11 scheduler: pod small-gpu-xyz scheduled -> node gpu-rack-42
I0315 09:10:11 kubelet: attach-volume delay 8.3s
I0315 09:10:26 scheduler: pod medium-gpu-abc pending due to insufficient resources
```

kai: re: bunching — I think the binpacker score is over-favoring pack-until-full for small pods. when small pods flood it fills a few nodes and leaves holes too big for medium. Combined with network attach jitter it's forcing preemptions.

maria: exact. also noticed a label mismatch: `gpu.size=small` vs `gpu.size=large` affinity isn't soft, it's strict on some deployments. that makes compaction worse.

liz: is this correlated with the new autoscaler burst config we rolled yesterday? it had 'prefer-small=true' fallback.

ajay: yes, autoscaler logs show surge of 90 small pods from job-queue at 09:05. policy: aggressive-burst. queue backlog -> burst -> pack -> attach delays -> eviction ripple.

sam: ops idea: introduce short-lived 'deprioritize-small-backfill' phase during bursts. basically prefer spreading small pods across warm nodes instead of filling new racks. flips binpacker weight for 60s.

kai: config prototype:
```
--scheduler-feature-gates=BinpackBalance=true
--binpack-balance.window=60s
--binpack-balance.weight.small=0.3
--binpack-balance.weight.large=0.8
```

maria: nice. also propose quick taint tweak: add taint `bunching=avoid:NoSchedule` to hot racks, and use tolerations only for medium/large-critical.

ajay: we should be careful: taints + preemptions might increase latency for PLG traffic. run canary in ap-southeast1-c first.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: started rollout of binpack-balance featureflag to kube-scheduler-canary (ap-southeast1-c) by kai

kai: I'll run canary for 2h during low traffic window 01:00-03:00 UTC. collecting evict metrics + network attach latency traces.

maria: action items: kai -> canary + telemetry; ajay -> collect attach latency histograms + autoscaler surge traces; liz -> review deploy policy for prefer-small toggle; sam -> sketch ops playbook for manual taint flip.

liz: +1. timeline — results by EOD tomorrow.

maria: thanks team. If we still see hotspots after config tweak, we may need to adjust instance selection (avoid same-az-rack at scale) — cost tradeoff but better SLOs.

ajay: noted. saving logs to: https://logs.redwood.example.com/gpu-prod-ap-se1/9412345678

sam: ping @oncall if anything regresses.
